task.description: Independent security gate on REQ-230's three-layer SQL-injection defence (closed operator enum -> allowlist-only column resolution -> positional-parameter binding) per docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8. Re-derived every claim from source rather than trusting ELIXIR-DEV's handoff: read types.ex/allowlist.ex/compiler.ex line by line, traced the allowlist->compiler call path, independently ran mix compile/mix test, and constructed 5 additional own injection probes (UNION-based payload, :in-list embedded injection, comment-sequence against an integer field, second-order/stored-then-filtered injection-shaped data, sort-field-name smuggling) beyond the delivered test suite's own AC4 coverage -- all 5 passed against a real Postgres tenant schema, then deleted (not part of the delivered artefact set).

result.note:
INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES (new query surface reading business data, S1/S2 preconditions met). SATISFIED: (a) compile/2 requires an explicit prefix and never calls Repo.* itself; the caller (test suite, future router) must pass prefix: schema_name to Repo.all/2 -- confirmed by reading compiler.ex:79-99 and by the AC5 cross-tenant test (query_test.exs:478-500) which compiles the identical request under two distinct tenant schemas and shows tenant B's query finds zero of tenant A's rows. (b) Allowlist.load/2 validates prefix via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 before any query -- read lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:194-209: this rejects any string not exactly 'tenant_' + 32 lowercase hex chars forming a valid UUID, so the prefix identifier itself cannot carry injection or cross-schema-reference characters regardless of caller input. (c) no migration in this diff (pure library modules, no priv/repo/migrations/ changes) -- N/A. All three verification points (a)/(b)/(c) confirmed directly against source, not the handoff's claims.

INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started; this diff adds no API route/controller, confirmed below).

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES (repo-wide check). grep -rn 'System.get_env' and the hardcoded-secret heuristic grep found no hits inside lib/letflow/entities/query/ or the new test file; no secret material touched by this diff. SATISFIED.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping) -- this handoff itself is the proof artefact; APPLIES and SATISFIED by this document.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, this is the core of the requirement. SATISFIED after line-by-line verification: every fragment/1 call in compiler.ex (json_cast_dynamic/2, lines 235-254) passes a @module_attribute (@string_fragment/@integer_fragment/@decimal_fragment/@boolean_fragment/@date_fragment/@datetime_fragment, each a fixed compile-time literal e.g. '?->>?', '(?->>?)::bigint') selected purely by pattern-matching on the closed Definition.field_type() atom -- never built via <>, to_string, or interpolation of caller data. Both fragment placeholders are bound as separate ^-parameters: r.field_values (the column) and ^field_name (the JSONB key, itself drawn only from Allowlist.load/2's finite, tenant-definition-derived key set, never a raw caller string) -- confirmed at compiler.ex:236,239,242,245,248,251,254. The comparison value is a further, always-separate ^value bind (compiler.ex:258-316). The only <> string-concatenation found (compiler.ex:205,210,298,304) builds the ILIKE *pattern text* ('%'<>value<>'%') which is itself then bound as a single ^pattern parameter to ilike/2 -- this is Elixir-side value-string construction, not SQL-text construction, and is not an injection vector (a caller's own literal '%'/'_' in the value only broadens pattern-matching semantics within the same tenant-scoped, already-authorized query -- it cannot execute arbitrary SQL, alter query structure, or cross tenant boundaries; noting this to REVIEWER as a minor non-blocking UX/precision observation, not a security defect). typed_column_dynamic/3's column reference always uses field(r, ^column_atom) where column_atom is sourced only from Allowlist.typed_columns/0's fixed table (allowlist.ex:62-73) via Map.fetch! -- never String.to_atom/1 on caller input, so no atom-exhaustion or arbitrary-column risk either. Traced full call path Compiler.compile/2 -> build_all_filter_dynamics/2 -> build_one_filter_dynamic/2 -> Allowlist.resolve_field/2 (field-not-allowed short-circuit, compiler.ex:358-366) -> Types-closed op already required at clause-construction -> build_filter_dynamic/2's exhaustive {source,op,type} pattern match with no catch-all clause (compiler.ex:163-179) -- no path skips allowlist resolution or reaches a fragment with an unvetted field name. Traced Types.parse_filter_op/1 (types.ex:81-97): a closed case statement over 12 literal strings, {:error,{:unknown_operator,raw}} on anything else -- no regex, no atom conversion of caller input, no way for an unrecognised operator string to reach the compiler.

Independently re-ran mix test test/letflow/entities/query_test.exs myself (26 tests, 0 failures, 25.0s) and specifically re-read AC4's 4 tests (query_test.exs:314-426): confirmed (a) they execute Repo.all(query, prefix: schema) against a real, non-mocked, sandboxed Postgres tenant schema provisioned via the same TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/1 path production code uses; (b) the DROP-TABLE payload test asserts Repo.aggregate(Latest, :count, prefix: schema) == 2 both before and after running the injection-payload query -- a real DROP TABLE succeeding would make this aggregate raise Postgrex.Error(undefined_table), so this is a genuine, non-tautological proof of non-execution; (c) re-ran and it passed again on this independent run.

Went beyond the existing suite: constructed and ran 5 of my own additional injection probes against a real Postgres tenant schema (in a temporary test file, deleted afterward -- not part of the delivered artefact set, per role instructions not to write the fix/tests myself): (1) a UNION SELECT payload naming every entity_record_latest column, against a string JSONB :eq filter -- matched zero rows, table intact. (2) an :in filter with a list containing an embedded "'; DROP TABLE ...; --" element -- matched zero rows, table intact (confirms Ecto's parameterised `in` over a caller-supplied list is also safe, not just scalar values). (3) a Postgres comment-sequence payload ("42 OR 1=1 --") against an :integer JSONB field -- rejected client-side by Postgrex/DBConnection's own type encoder (DBConnection.EncodeError) before a single byte reached the wire; table intact. (4) second-order injection: stored a record whose customer_name value is itself SQL-shaped text ("Robert'); DROP TABLE entity_record_latest;--"), then filtered for that exact value -- round-tripped as plain string equality, returned exactly the one matching row, table intact throughout. (5) attempted field-name smuggling via the sort clause (a DROP-TABLE-shaped string as the sort `field`) -- rejected at the allowlist with {:field_not_allowed, ...} before any query was built; table intact. All 5 passed on first correct run (test 3 initially failed only because my own rescue clause's exception list was incomplete -- DBConnection.EncodeError vs. the Postgrex.Error/FunctionClauseError set the delivered suite's analogous :decimal test rescues; this is a difference in which client-side type-validation exception class Postgrex raises for :integer vs :numeric targets, not a security gap, and was in my probe code, not the reviewed code). Could not construct a working injection against this compiler through any value position, the JSONB key position, the sort-field position, the :in-list position, or the typed-column position.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES. SATISFIED: compile/2's with-chain (compiler.ex:86-98) and every nested with-chain (build_one_filter_dynamic/2, build_filter_dynamic/2, load/2, fetch_active_definition/2) use typed {:ok,_}/{:error,_} tuples throughout with no bare pattern match on an external-I/O or caller-controlled result; grep -rn '^\s*{:ok, .*} = ' lib/letflow/entities/query/ found zero hits. The one place a raw exception can surface (Postgrex's client-side type-encoding rejection on a malformed numeric-typed filter value, e.g. AC4's :decimal test and my own :integer probe) is Postgrex's own defence layer triggering before any SQL is sent -- this is an accepted, explicitly-designed outcome per AC4's own wording ('treated as inert data ... or errors cleanly'), not an unhandled-crash defect, and it occurs at the Repo.all/2 call site the eventual router will own (compile/2 itself never raises on any malformed request I could construct -- confirmed by the AC5 error-taxonomy test and by my own 5 probes, none of which raised inside compile/2, only (in one case) inside the subsequent Repo.all/2 call).

INV-9 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (no outbound HTTP request, no tenant-controlled URL in this diff).

Structural: git diff main...HEAD --stat -- 'lib/letflow_web/*' 'lib/**/router*' returned no hits -- confirmed no route/controller was added or modified; this compiler backs a deferred router per the design, matching AC6.

Ran myself, all green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean), mix format --check-formatted (clean), mix test test/letflow/entities/query_test.exs (26 tests, 0 failures), mix test test/letflow/entities/ (129 tests, 0 failures, full regression). base_commit 0f5710f8 matches main's current HEAD -- diff is exactly this requirement's additions plus its own handoff files.

No BLOCKER found on any applicable invariant. One non-blocking observation forwarded to REVIEWER (not a security defect, so not grounds for FAIL): the :contains/:starts_with ILIKE pattern-building (compiler.ex:204-212,296-306) does not escape a caller-supplied literal '%' or '_' inside the filter value before wrapping it in wildcards -- this only changes which rows match within the same tenant-scoped, already-authorized query (e.g. a value of '%' matches every row for that field) and cannot execute SQL, alter query structure, or cross a tenant boundary, so it is a query-precision nit for REVIEWER's idiom pass, not an SQL-injection or tenant-isolation gap.
